content:
Although I usually prefer using my iPhone naked—without a case or screen protector—I am actually using both on my iPhone 17 Pro, and I can recommend them to everyone. Neither accessory is expensive, so you can buy them and give them a try; if they don't suit you, you don't have to keep them on permanently.

Five years ago, Apple introduced Ceramic Shield glass to the iPhone display, claiming a four-fold improvement in drop test performance and promising that iPhone screens would be less prone to shattering.

My iPhone screen has yet to crack, but after about a year of use, two or three deep scratches always end up appearing on the display.

This year's Ceramic Shield 2 front glass claims a three-fold improvement in scratch resistance.

Apple also says the front panel has enhanced anti-reflective properties this time, but compared to the nano-texture anti-glare treatment on the iPad Pro and MacBook Pro, the gap is still significant.

Giving your iPhone 17 Pro display a more matte finish

For the above reasons, I went back to a product I tried a few years ago and found quite good—namely, Mothca's matte glass screen protector.

This product is not perfect. If there were an iPhone with nano-texture without that slight rainbow effect and drop in brightness, I would be even more satisfied.

However, if you're interested in a matte screen effect, I still recommend giving it a try—especially since the single or twin pack is only US$9 or US$14. The feel of the product seems far more premium than its price suggests.

A slim case suitable for 'just in case'

Now let's talk about iPhone cases. I don't want to spend too much on a case, because I don't plan to use one every day.

I usually only put a case on before activities like kayaking or mounting my iPhone on a motorcycle handlebar. I also worry that the sharp corners of the camera bump might scratch the orange aluminum frame.

I like black, but feel that black paired with Cosmic Orange used every day has a bit of a Halloween vibe. So I decided to go for a greyer option that matches the orange, creating a kind of futuristic spacesuit feel.

I picked up this case at a retail store a few days ago on a whim, and found it very satisfying.

This is the Thin Fit case from Spigen, available in black, Tungsten Grey, or Deep Sea Green. I went with the grey one, and it feels just right for the look I had in mind.

Spigen prices it at US$39.99, though Amazon sells the same case for just US$34.99.

I've noticed many budget cases don't have built-in MagSafe, which affects the performance of external battery packs and magnetic mounts.

The Spigen Thin Fit has built-in MagSafe, plus a capacitive Camera Control cover rather than just a cutout.

I like that this case fully encloses the entire camera 'plateau', because durability in that area is what concerns me most.

Once fitted, it also creates a rather stylish 'orange ring' look, somewhat reminiscent of the Digital Crown on the Space Black Apple Watch Ultra.

Apart from the port at the bottom, the Cosmic Orange also shows through along the edges of the button covers, achieving the orange accent against grey effect I was after.

Another benefit is that, once the case is on, you no longer see the orange aluminum frame around the display. Without the case, it looks fine, but with a dark case on, you end up with just a thin orange strip separating the black case from the black display, which I find quite jarring.

Two budget iPhone 17 Pro accessory recommendations

The Mothca screen protector can help you avoid deep scratches, and if you like an anti-glare display, the matte feel is also excellent. The Spigen Thin Fit case has a metallic feel, is smooth to the touch, and won't make the device too bulky.

Make the most of your Apple products
